records.title: Products of the Two Focal Inversion Areas in Elliptic Billiards
records.description:
For every odd-periodic real billiard family in an ellipse, we prove that the product of the trajectory-order signed areas of the two polygons obtained by unit inversion of the original vertices about the two original boundary foci is a positive phase-independent constant. The result includes every primitive odd period, admitted coprime star winding, orientation reversal and fixed odd repeated traversal; an r-fold traversal multiplies the product by r^2. Circular boundaries are treated directly. A real-caustic parity lemma excludes an omitted nondegenerate odd hyperbolic or degenerate family. In confocal Jacobi coordinates, each inverse-area trace has at most simple poles. For odd periods the two focal pole sets are disjoint, and reversal forces the opposite trace to vanish at each possible pole. Their product is therefore holomorphic on a compact quotient torus and constant. Real geometry establishes positive areas and finite inversion vertices.

The target is invariant k903,a in arXiv:2004.12497v11, corresponding to frozen record AMR-050-0062 / 5100062. Reznik, Garcia and Helman's published N=3 formula is expressly credited, together with the classical Jacobi parametrization and meromorphic method. Exact controls verify the common product 1/324 for two non-equivalent triangular phases in one fixed family, odd-repeat scaling and a separate circle case. Genuine period-four phases instead give products 1 and 25/16, showing that the odd hypothesis cannot be removed. A separately executed 85-decimal diagnostic samples 42 odd-period families, including 27 stars, at five phases each; these finite checks are not the general proof. The quantity is signed area in trajectory order, not the unsigned area of a self-crossed polygon's bounded faces. This English preprint is AI-assisted, originating-researcher self-audited and unrefereed. Novelty remains undetermined; no independent human review, proof-assistant verification, guaranteed indexing or absolute-priority claim is made.

records.title: Full 5-torsion of the regular-pentagon quintic pencil
records.description:
This research note computes all twenty-five geometric fifth-torsion points of the genus-one normalization of the regular-pentagon quintic pencil in McCallum's Question 17 in the AIM workshop problem list on rational and integral points. For an explicit equation normalization over K=Q(sqrt(5)), it gives a cubic model, both birational maps, a degree-ten residual polynomial and both ordinate branches. The complete division field is K(sqrt(5+2sqrt(5)),zeta_5,theta), where theta^5=lambda+phi^5 and phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2. Its degree is four or twenty, with the exact splitting criterion and Galois action specified. The computation covers every elliptic normalization, including the allowed cuspidal plane member.

The proof applies classical Tate normal form, Fisher's full-level modular cover, Verdure's full-torsion specialization criterion, Morton's prior explicit Tate torsion formulas and residual polynomial, division-polynomial theory and the Weil pairing. It credits the source's known infinity subgroup and the earlier partial computation. No first-discovery or first-priority claim is made. records.title: Closedness and attractive approximation of binary MTP2 edge models
records.description:
For every fixed finite simple graph, this research note proves that the binary MTP2 probability distributions admitting finite nonnegative unary and original-edge factors are exactly the pointwise limits of strictly positive attractive Ising distributions on the same graph. It consequently answers Conjecture 1 in Lauritzen's 2022 Oberwolfach problem statement affirmatively, including zero probabilities and the source's literal edge-only conventions for isolated vertices and empty graphs. The proof explicitly handles pins, deterministic equalities and implication supports, aggregates interactions across equality classes, constructs positive attractive approximations, and uses a classical residual-flow representation to bound finite factors with a nonvanishing normalizer.

The note credits the toric support framework of Geiger, Meek and Sturmfels, the MTP2 graphical results of Lauritzen, Uhler and Zwiernik and Fallat et al., the natural-support factorization framework of Kahle and Sullivant, and classical graph-cut and residual-flow tools. The supplement gives the additional facial-lattice support derivation underlying the comparison. The accompanying negative answers to the separate factorization conjectures are credited to the exact earlier counterexample of Gandolfi and Lenarda, published April 13, 2017. No new-counterexample, first-discovery or exhaustive historical-priority claim is made. Portable exact verification code and generated results accompany the proofs; bounded finite checks do not replace the arbitrary-graph proof.

This is an unrefereed preprint. AI tools were used extensively in developing the arguments, searching primary literature, writing, coding, reproduction and independent adversarial review. records.title: Output-sensitive sparse factorization over finite fields from dense factorization
records.description: We give a deterministic reduction for complete sparse univariate polynomial factorization over explicitly represented finite fields. The bit cost is polynomial in term count, binary exponent length, field encoding and the total degree of the distinct densely returned factors, with arbitrary binary multiplicities. A sparse numerator and dense denominator are maintained through characteristic-p descent; denominator degree grows by at most the original radical degree per step. Classical Pade reconstruction, logarithmic derivatives, residue multiplicity methods and Cartier sections are attributed to their original sources. The paper also details inherited dense factorization and prescribed-degree irreducible construction consequences of OpenAI family142 through Berlekamp, Shoup and Rai. records.title: The Elements with Property (s) of a Skew Brace Need Not Form an Ideal: On a Question of Colazzo, Ferrara and Trombetti
records.description:
An element x of a skew brace B has property (s), in the sense of Colazzo, Ferrara and Trombetti, if it has only finitely many conjugates of each of the kinds x∗b, b∗x, b+x−b and b∘x∘b⁻¹. In her abstract in Oberwolfach Report 9/2023, Colazzo asks whether the elements with property (s) of a skew brace form an ideal; by a result of the three authors they do so in two-sided braces. We answer the question in the negative. On Z × Z/4, with componentwise addition, the multiplication (m,a)∘(n,b) = (m + ε(a)n, a + b + 2ab), where ε(a) = 1 for a ∈ {0,1} and ε(a) = −1 for a ∈ {2,3}, defines a left brace in which the elements with property (s) are those of Z × {0,1}; this set is not closed under addition and not invariant under the maps λ_b. A sub-brace with additive group Z × Z/2 has the same property. The verification is elementary and is given in full. On the positive side, in every skew brace these elements form a normal subgroup of the multiplicative group, so only the additive conditions can fail; and they form an ideal in two-sided skew braces, in braces with torsion-free additive group, in bi-skew braces, and in skew braces whose multiplicative group is an FC-group. In semidirect products of a trivial brace by a finite skew brace Q the set in question is given by a normal subgroup of the multiplicative group of Q, which can be prescribed; this yields examples for each way in which the additive conditions can fail, among them a skew brace with torsion-free additive group, a centrally nilpotent brace of exponent 4, and the structure skew brace of a non-degenerate solution of the Yang–Baxter equation with six elements. The question, the notion and the positive answer for two-sided braces are due to Colazzo, Ferrara and Trombetti; the brace on Z/4 underlying the example is Example 3.8 of their paper, and the semidirect product of skew braces is a known construction. That the elements with property (s) form a subgroup of the multiplicative group follows at once from a characterisation in a recent preprint of Di Matteo and Ferrara together with a result of Cascella, Properzi and Van Antwerpen; it also follows from a result of Mondal and Yadav on a set which we show to be the same. The statement on two-sided skew braces is a short consequence of the first two results. Our proofs are included for completeness. The example also shows that Lemma 3.12 of the paper of Colazzo, Ferrara and Trombetti needs an additional hypothesis; it holds for skew braces with property (S), where it is used. The literature was searched within the limits stated in the text (one citing paper was seen in abstract only). A search that finds nothing is not a proof of novelty, and no priority is claimed. This is an unrefereed note.

records.title: A counterexample to ideal closure of property-(s) elements in skew braces
records.description:

records.title: A regular zero-area singularity with a nonzero weak Bianchi defect
records.description:
We give a counterexample to the geometric regular-zero-area-singularity implication in the Oberwolfach report conjecture (problem 30004807 / OWR-8415343-010), under the cited Burtscher-Kiessling-Tahvildar-Zadeh convention of smooth compactly supported vector fields reaching the retained inner boundary and regularity of the static spacelike slices. The spacetime is a negative-mass specialization of the known Dadhich-Kar-Mukherjee-Visser metric, whose tensor formulas are credited. Its static slices have harmonically regular zero-area singularities of mass -2a. We prove absolute convergence of the complete weak Bianchi scalar for every permitted test and compute an explicit nonzero boundary functional, with value -8 pi for a normalized radial test. The boundary-flux method is credited to the existing literature; convergence is established directly, without invoking a sufficient theorem outside its hypotheses.

The example violates the null energy condition. records.title: NP-completeness of three-terminal shortest-path blocking
records.description:
We prove NP-completeness of undirected, unit-traversal-length three-terminal Blocking Shortest Paths: delete a minimum edge set to increase every pairwise terminal distance by at least one. Hardness holds with unit deletion costs and all three original terminal distances equal to three. A direct Vertex Cover reduction also proves NP-completeness when all terminal distances must remain finite, or increase exactly from three to four. The result classifies the undirected triangle question posed by Stefan Krause in 2005. The classical subdivision identity is credited to Poljak (1974), and the related tripartite attachment mechanism to Khachiyan and coauthors (2008). Historical first priority and continued open status through 2026 are not asserted.

This unrefereed research note includes a source and verification archive with the unchanged original proof packet, explicit hash manifests, source-free standard-library Python reproduction, independent adversarial mathematical and computational audits, source-model checks and a bounded priority audit. AI tools were used extensively for construction, verification, adversarial review and writing. records.title: Verification of the odd-period focal inversion area product
records.description: Attributed verification/research note giving a self-contained flag-curve proof of the historical odd-period focal inversion signed-area product: k903,a in Reznik--Garcia--Koiller arXiv:2004.12497v11 and Conjecture 1 of Reznik--Garcia--Helman arXiv:2012.03020v2. Alper Ferudun, Products of the Two Focal Inversion Areas in Elliptic Billiards, version 1.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23096994, proves the same theorem using substantially the same meromorphic divisor mechanism; this exact overlap and the established general method are explicitly credited. The strict theorem concerns proper confocal nested ellipses, original ordered vertices, original foci, unit inversion, signed straight-edge areas, every admitted coprime winding of a primitive odd-period orbit, reversal and indexed repetitions. A portable standard-library exact verifier accompanies four specified convex winding-one controls, with actual normal/optimized receipts and deliberate negative controls; finite checks do not prove the all-period theorem. The source ZIP includes authored source, code and notes, without third-party full texts or dependencies. The bounded priority comparison leaves documented access gaps and does not establish novelty, first proof, certified independent discovery, literal simultaneity, absolute priority or current openness. Specified PR/commit and Zenodo record dates are reported with these limitations. AI tools were used extensively in research, proof development, drafting, auditing and computation. Separate AI adversarial checks are not independent human peer review. This is an unrefereed research note without conventional human refereeing or proof-assistant certification.
